quarantine.independentReview: Intersection x has 35−x Carrom-only, 20−x Chess-only and x−5 neither. All are nonnegative exactly for integers 5 through 20. Both reader languages correctly give the range and explain the condition for 5.
Division gives p(x)=(x−a)Q(x)+p(a). If p(a)=0, x−a is both a divisor and a factor. Both reader languages identify choices (1) and (4).
Distinct primes have GCD 1, while gcd(2,2)=2. The two editions omit distinctness. Both reader languages correctly present the two cases.

For the intended acute right-triangle model, cos θ=b/√(a²+b²) and both products are ab/√(a²+b²). Without positive b, a=3, b=−4 and acute sin θ=3/5 give −12/5 and 12/5. Both reader languages show the same valid condition and counterexample.
2θ=60° or 120° yields θ=30° or 60° within the acute-angle interpretation. Both are printed options. No reader card.
The first term equals 3. The second equals 2 cos(41°)/cos(51°), giving approximately 5.3984908 in total. None of 2, 3, 5, 6 is exact. Both languages print the same angles. No reader card.
Surface area is 6s². The areas have ratio 4:9 and 16:36 is equivalent. Both reader languages correctly explain both options.

With AP difference d, the expression is x^(−d)y^(2d)z^(−d). Positive bases permit (y²/(xz))^d=1. Taking a,b,c=0,1/2,1 and x=y=z=−1 makes the printed real expression undefined. The positive-base proof is sound in both reader languages.
English Vieta gives p²/q²−2r/q=−p²/q², hence p²=qr. Tamil reverses the premise. For q=1,p=−1,r=0, x²+x has roots 0,−1 and their squares are roots of x²−x, yet (1,−1,0) fails p²=qr. No reader card.
BD+DC=5, so AB+BC=10=AC. The triangle is degenerate. Also 3/7 differs from 1/2. The bilingual diagnosis is correct.

Take D at 0, B at −a/2, C at a/2 and E at signed coordinate t. Then b²=p²−at+a²/4. Printed plus sign requires t=−x (or x=0); t=+x reverses it. The paired pages supply neither order nor figure for Q6. No reader card.
With the same signed coordinate t, c²=p²+at+a²/4. The printed minus sign requires t=−x (or x=0). Their sum in part iii is unaffected. No reader card for ii.
D and E fix no F. If D,E,F are internal and CD, AE, BF are concurrent, Ceva gives (5/3)(3/2)(CF/FA)=1 and CF=6 from AC=21. The concurrency is absent in both. No reader card.

AB and CD are horizontal. The BC and DA equations intersect at (6,−25/4), interior to both segments. Under order ABDC the other two slopes are 3/2 and −3/2. The bilingual reader correctly distinguishes both orders.

Since (sin θ+cos θ)²≤2 for real θ, no real angle satisfies the premise. Formally the premise gives sin θ cos θ=1 and hence the printed algebraic consequence 1. Both reader languages explain the impossibility.

All solutions have θ=30°+180°k. Then 3θ=90°+540°k and tan(3θ) is undefined. On the right, tan²θ=1/3 gives a zero denominator and nonzero numerator. Both reader languages correctly demonstrate the acute representative.
Monotonicity requires P(A∪B)≥2/3, contradicted by 1/3. Formal inclusion–exclusion yields 11/15>min(2/3,2/5), another contradiction. Both editions agree on the incompatible data. No reader card.
For N=10k+r pages numbered 1 through N, favourable count is 7k+min(r,6). For N=10 it gives 7/10; for N=9 it gives 2/3. Both editions omit N. No reader card.

The V1.5 holdout is visible in the same source file. Thirty expected sets are computed with TypedSet, also used by the system under test. This is a correlated oracle.
